quotes.text: I’ve been on both sides of a paycheck. I know what it’s like to sign one and what it’s like to depend on one. Right now, AI and automation are changing jobs faster than Washington is reacting. That’s a problem. Workers, not just tech companies, deserve a voice in what comes next.

Mark Zuckerberg continues to put profits over the safety of children through his company’s reckless policies. I look forward to working in Congress to hold social media conglomerates accountable and create policies that regulate AI technology and protect children.

https://t.co/MvigNf1132

At today’s @EdWorkforceDems hearing, I outlined concerns about AI use in the classroom and the biases it introduces for disadvantaged students. I also stressed that when it comes to technology and education, our first priority must always be the safety and wellbeing of students. https://t.co/B3CRvlaJIK

At today’s @EdWorkforceDems hearing, I outlined my concerns over the use of AI and the inequities it can exacerbate. It’s critical that we don’t leave workers behind or sacrifice them for a future with AI. https://t.co/E7U2uDoftc
Artificial intelligence, or AI, has rapidly been introduced into Americans’ lives. While some uses of this technology in the workplace show promise, it also poses significant dangers.

Congress has a responsibility to rein in big tech companies who take advantage of this prosperity and potential benefits so that AI can be used for everybody - for workers instead of against them. We don’t need another tool that will funnel profits to the ultra-wealthy at the expense of working Americans. Congress must take an active role in shaping how AI is integrated into our lives and in developing thoughtful regulations that balance protecting workers with fostering economic growth.

At today’s @EdWorkforceDems Labor Subcommittee hearing, I shared my deep concerns about the way AI has been used to suppress wages and to retaliate against workers who are trying to unionize. As this new technology becomes increasingly present in our workplaces, it is critical that we put in place guardrails to protect workers and their rights.

This week I voted against the ICE funding bill and have called to abolish the broken institution. Tune in for more on this and my thoughts on protecting workers and their privacy from AI. https://t.co/LCXLDTpOxS

The wealth gap between big corporations and the working people who make these companies’ success possible has been widening for decades and will only be exacerbated by the unchecked rise of AI. As a senior member @EdWorkforceDems, I’m pushing my colleagues in Congress to act now to protect American workers by both implementing commonsense guardrails on AI and ensuring the ultrawealthy pay their fair share.
https://t.co/LqxGxCqdxi

I appreciated the opportunity to sit down yesterday afternoon with brilliant researchers at the @UCBLaborCenter to discuss the ongoing challenges posed by the emergence of AI in the workplace. In committee hearings @EdWorkforceDems, we have already been strategizing legislative pathways to protect American workers, their privacy, and American jobs, and yesterday’s conversation armed me with more ideas for approaching this complex challenge. It’s always enlightening to visit one of the top public research universities in the world!

As our civil rights are under relentless attack from the Trump Administration, I am prouder than ever to receive a 100% scorecard from @ACLU. Whether it be standing up for free speech or regulating AI to protect privacy, I’m committed to protecting your rights and freedoms in Congress.
https://t.co/36ulOgbayy

At today’s @EdWorkforceDems hearing, I raised concerns about the changing job market with the widespread adoption of AI both here in the Bay Area and across the country. As a senior member on this committee, I am eager to work on bipartisan legislation to address these changes to the workforce and ensure Americans are protected and prepared for the jobs of the future.

In today’s @EdWorkforceDems Higher Education Subcommittee hearing, I outlined my concerns about the impact of AI on the mental health and social development of college students. It’s critical we do all we can to protect the wellbeing of our nation’s future leaders. https://t.co/z9TqBrx6Sw

We had two big hearings last week in @EdWorkforceDems – one about the emergence of AI in higher education and the importance of protecting students’ wellbeing, the other about the only federal agency responsible for protecting the rights and right to organize of American workers. Tune in to hear about those hearings and two town halls I am looking forward to hosting.

I echo the concerns of public health experts and mental health professionals who are sounding the alarm about Americans, especially young people, turning to AI chatbots for behavioral health services. It is past time for Congress to impose guardrails on this technology to protect Americans who are struggling with their mental health.
Trump’s DHS posted an overtly racist and bigoted AI graphic targeting Sikh-Americans based solely on their background and faith. This is disgraceful and un-American.

It’s past time for Congress to pass meaningful AI safeguards to protect the American people. I joined more than 100 of my colleagues this week in calling on Speaker Johnson to keep Congress in Washington and let us do our jobs and vote on AI safeguards. https://t.co/7ogi7kubZY

One thing about Congress many Americans may not be aware of is that the majority party, in this case Republicans, controls the congressional calendar. Once again, Republican leadership is sending us home early rather than voting to lower costs for Americans, regulate the AI industry, or impeach Secretary Hegseth for his disastrous handling of the illegal Iran war. Tune in to our weekly video to hear more about the Republican majority’s absolute inability to govern and solve problems for the American people.

In @EdWorkforceDems, we have been working to address the concerning rise of wrongful health insurance disputes and denials thanks to AI. Not only is it immoral, but it is driving up healthcare costs for all Americans. We must address this now.
https://t.co/N5ddfoTYvJ

If you missed yesterday’s Town Hall on Social Media and Mental Health, we discussed the challenges of keeping kids safe online, especially with the rise of AI, how to identify if you or your child are being negatively impacted by social media use, and more. 

A big thank you to our fantastic expert special guests Dr. Supreet Mann from @CommonSense and Dr. Brian Keum from UC Berkeley for sharing the latest data on the link between social media and mental health. You can watch a recording of the conversation here: https://t.co/pZRd6HQHjW
